'''Ritva Serimaa''' (née Ström) (September 20, 1957, [[Hamina]] – April 12, 2016, Hamina) was a [[Finland|Finnish]] physicist and professor, the first female professor of physics at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref name="Huotari 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.hs.fi/ihmiset/art-2000002902214.html|title=Fysiikan professori tutki myös Vasa-laivaa|last=Huotari|first=Simo|date=May 21, 2016|work=Helsingin Sanomat|access-date=13 July 2018}}</ref> She gained her master's degree in 1982 and defended her doctoral thesis in 1990, becoming a [[docent]] of the University of Helsinki in 1992. Her doctoral thesis work and later research concerned [[X-ray]] physics and [[scattering]]. From 1991 to 1993 she worked at [[Stanford University]] making use of their [[synchrotron light source]] [[Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource|SSRL]]. One research focus was the structure of the preserved [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[warship]] [[Vasa (ship)|Vasa]], whose structure was at risk due to damage from [[sulfur]]-containing compounds. From 2004 she was professor of physics at the [[University of Helsinki]], the first woman to hold such a post.<ref name="Huotari 2018" />

Serimaa supervised 16 doctoral theses and published at least 230 peer-reviewed articles. In 2010 she was made a member of the [[Suomalainen Tiedeakatemia|Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]]. In 2011 she became the first female chair of the [[Finnish Physical Society]].<ref name="Huotari 2018" /><ref>[http://www.acadsci.fi/jasenet/uudet_jasenet.htm Suomalainen tiedeakatemia]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fyysikkoseura.fi/aiemmin.html |title=Suomen Fyysikkoseura |access-date=July 13, 2018 |archive-date=May 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521140406/http://www.fyysikkoseura.fi/aiemmin.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Serimaa married the physicist Olli Serimaa in 1982.<ref name="Huotari 2018" />
